Single-objective optimization · SETTING 58

Exact comparison feedback for smooth convex objectives

SO_ZO_O01

Minimize a globally smooth convex objective using exact comparisons. Deterministic and randomized fixed-budget complexities agree up to logarithmic factors throughout the documented joint domain $Q=\beta R^2/\varepsilon\ge32$.

01

Setting specification

Task

Minimize $f$ globally over $\mathbb{R}^d$ and return a point with small objective gap.

Admissible model

$f:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is differentiable and satisfies $\|\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y)\|_2\le\beta\|x-y\|_2$ for every $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$.

$f$ is globally convex.

A global minimizer $x_*\in B_2(0,R)$ exists; the localization ball does not restrict the function domain.

Oracle interface

Any finite point pair $(x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}^d$ may be queried, returning $\operatorname{sign}(f(x)-f(y))\in\{-1,0,1\}$. Equal values produce zero. Neither the magnitude of the difference nor either function value is revealed.

The public inputs are $d$, $\beta$, $R$, $\varepsilon$, together with the sets, kernels and auxiliary operations explicitly declared above. Information about the unknown objective and any undisclosed sample distribution is obtained only through the stated interface.

Output

Return $\widehat{x}\in \mathbb{R}^d$. The output may be an unqueried point, an average or convex combination that remains in the stated space. No function value, gradient, inner solution, or accuracy certificate must accompany the output.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The base loss is $\ell(I,x)=f(x)-f_*$, where $f_*=\inf_{u\in \mathbb{R}^d}f(u)$. This nonnegative loss is evaluated at the output, with tolerance $\varepsilon$.

Resource accounting

One point-pair comparison costs $1$ call. Every repeated comparison and every comparison in a line search is charged. The budget $T$ counts scalar comparison replies.

Only the declared oracle resource is charged. Computation and storage using existing information, together with explicitly known geometric and proximal operations, are free.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Deterministic

Only deterministic strategies are allowed. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The requirement $\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon$ holds deterministically for each instance.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Randomized

Private randomization is allowed, with the seed independent of the instance and external randomness. Queries, stopping and postprocessing may be arbitrary measurable adaptive functions of the history. No linear-span or zero-respecting restriction is imposed.

Interactions are sequential, and every actual response in a batch is charged separately. Except for explicitly listed auxiliary interfaces, arithmetic, linear algebra, storage, and internal computation on available information are free, with no additional communication or memory restriction. Finite-difference steps must be finite and positive; real-number precision is not charged separately.

After fixing the public inputs, choose one algorithm that works for every admissible instance and reply law. The error requirement is $\Pr(\ell(I,\widehat{x})\le \varepsilon)\ge2/3$.

Probability is over the algorithm's random seed only.

Oracle cost uses a deterministic worst-case budget: $N\le T$ on every possible execution path. For multiple resources, coordinatewise caps apply jointly along the same path.

Output qualification. Random selection among previously queried points is permitted, subject to the declared success guarantee.

Domain
Take the supremum over Euclidean unit input vectors of the corresponding order.

$\|T\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|u_1\|_2,\ldots,\|u_j\|_2\le1}|T[u_1,\ldots,u_j]|$

$\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{fun}},\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}},\mathcal{X}$

Function domain, admissible output domain and optimization domain

Domain
Each is the Euclidean space or subset explicitly specified in this profile

$\mathcal{X}_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\mathcal{X}=\mathbb{R}^d$; the function domain is the region on which the model imposes regularity.

$N^*$

Optimal worst-case oracle complexity satisfying the complete guarantee

Domain
$N^*\in[0,+\infty]$

Take the infimum over admissible algorithms, followed by the worst case over the instances of this profile. With multiple resources, use this scalar only for an explicitly specified resource projection.

$x_*$

A global minimizer or quadratic center whose existence is promised by the model

Domain
Belongs to the localization domain specified here; used only under the stated existence promise

The full-space minimizer is unique in the strongly convex class. The center of a positive semidefinite quadratic model need not be unique.

Near-Optimal Smooth Convex Optimization with a Comparison Oracle ↗
Conditions
$d\ge1$; $\beta,R,\varepsilon>0$; $Q=\beta R^2/\varepsilon\ge1$.
Correspondence, constants and qualifications
Oracle correspondence
One native ternary reply implements the source bit $1\{f(x)\ge f(y)\}$: map 0 and +1 to 1, and -1 to 0. All queries remain finite full-space pairs.
Guarantee conversion
Deterministic objective gap at most $\varepsilon$ on every instance. The same strategy gives probability one under the randomized view, hence satisfies its per-instance 2/3 guarantee.
Output rule
The output is an arbitrary finite full-space iterate; it need not lie in the localization ball and no objective value or optimality certificate accompanies it.
Resource conversion
The prescribed horizon $K=\lceil10\sqrt Q\rceil$ and fixed inner schedules count every comparison. Lemma F.1 also bounds the number on every possible reply sequence.
Branch condition

All actual gradient/comparison calls are counted; no hidden oracle access. See complete proof ZO_PROOF_COMPARE_CENTROID_20261116
Branch condition
d integer>=1; beta,R,epsilon>0; Q=beta R^2/epsilon>=32.
Gap or comparison
$O\!\left(\frac{\min\{\sqrt Q[d\log(2dQ)+\log^2(2Q)],d^2\log Q\log(dQ)\}}{d\max\{d,\log Q\}}\right)\le O(\min\{d,\log Q\}\log(dQ))$.

/proofs/0/body · SHA-256 9fd8fd145f57cee534298bc780f287636c06f0076521ee2aeb2b63f7af047089
Two exact scalar values simulate one comparison. Therefore a fixed-success exact-value lower bound $L$ gives a comparison lower bound $L/2$. Expected-error targets require a separate constant-factor accuracy conversion. At each adaptive comparison request $(x,y)$, query both exact values and return their order, including the declared tie convention. The same seed and transcript generate the same next query and output, using at most twice the comparison budget. Hence a comparison algorithm contradicts a value lower theorem only when all source model and guarantee conditions match. For smooth convex objectives, apply the dimension/accuracy branch of Dorn et al., Theorem 2.1, at $Q\ge32$, and its logarithmic strongly convex subclass at $Q\ge128^2$; maximize only on their common window. For a strongly convex model with initial gap $\Delta$, choose a hard-instance radius $R_h=\sqrt{2\Delta/\beta}$. Smoothness at the global minimizer gives the required initial gap. If the target guarantee is expected error $\varepsilon$, Markov supplies success $2/3$ at error $3\varepsilon$; then the source scale is $Q_h=2\Delta/(3\varepsilon)$ and must be at least 32. No new public radius is added to the target specification. For nonconvex gradient stationarity, use the exact-value hard subclass with a proof-only Lipschitz budget satisfying $L^2\ge\beta\Delta$. The source cap $B=\min\{\beta\Delta,L^2\}$ becomes $\beta\Delta$. Retain its small-gradient window and dimension requirement $d\ge C(\beta\Delta/\varepsilon^2)\log(2+\beta\Delta/\varepsilon^2)$. The same two-value simulation then gives the registered comparison lower bound.

/proofs/1/body · SHA-256 4a3548e45d58d9b6b73488f7030fbfc7365e45f8db4f4bf616cd18096e865841
Primary source read: 2405.11454v1 Lemma 1 (directional preference), Theorem 1 and Theorem 2/Problem 1. PDF SHA256 150ea20d6fd61257782c67fe15fe135ee03ab828d84a3dc26f236b57ef4ac6c3, chars10500-14500 and14000-24000; HTML SHA256 354e38c235a5dcb24fca2e74ae4363767de6e27a0b8480b5240b30802d99a57a, chars25000-35000 verifies Theorems2-3 formulas. Source n=d,L=beta. A native tie0 is mapped to +1, an allowed source tie reply. Finite positive probes and Euclidean projection use only native public inputs; no value or certificate is obtained. The following explicit estimator supplies the needed direction guarantee independently of implementation details in source Algorithm2. Complete direction-estimation construction: Given delta in(0,1], gamma>0, use tolerance tau=delta gamma/(100d^2). A comparison at (x+(2tau/beta)v,x), for unit v, yields either <grad f(x),v>>=-tau or <grad f(x),v><=tau; this follows immediately from the smoothness Taylor remainder bounded by beta h^2/2, and is source Lemma1. Orient each basis vector v_i=+/-e_i using this test, so a_i=<grad f,v_i>>=-tau. Find a pivot p by a sequential tournament: compare components with direction (v_i-v_j)/sqrt(2); the selected winner is at least the loser minus sqrt(2)tau. If ||grad f||>=gamma, max a_i>=||grad f||/sqrt(d), and the final pivot a_p>=max a_i-sqrt(2)(d-1)tau>=gamma/(2sqrt(d))>0. Moreover each ratio r_i=a_i/a_p lies in[-2,2], because a_i>=-tau and a_i<=a_p+2d tau. For i!=p bisect [-2,2] using the directional test on (z v_p-v_i)/sqrt(1+z^2). Each reply compares z with r_i up to kappa=sqrt(5)tau/a_p<=2sqrt(5)sqrt(d)tau/gamma<=delta/(16sqrt(d)). Keep the indicated half interval; inductively the true r_i stays within distance kappa of it. After K=ceil(log_2(32sqrt(d)/delta)) rounds, its midpoint alpha_i satisfies |alpha_i-r_i|<=2/2^K+kappa<=delta/(8sqrt(d)). Set alpha_p=1. The vector r=(a_i/a_p) has norm>=1; ||alpha-r||<=delta/8. The elementary normalization inequality ||u/||u||-v/||v||||<=2||u-v||/||v|| shows that h=(sum alpha_i v_i)/||alpha|| differs from grad f/||grad f|| by at most delta/4, hence at most delta. For d=1 the ratio loop is empty and the oriented sign is correct under the promise. With or without the promise, the schedule has d+(d-1)+(d-1)K=O(d log(d/delta)) comparisons and returns a unit vector because alpha_p=1. Every probing radius is positive and finite, and no unbounded line search occurs. Complete uniform optimization derivation: Let Q=beta R^2/epsilon>=32, T=ceil(128Q), delta=1/(16 sqrt(Q)), gamma=epsilon/(2R), eta=R/sqrt(T). Start x_0=0; at each t=0,...,T-1 get unit h_t from the explicit fixed-schedule estimator above and set x_{t+1}=Proj_{B_R}(x_t-eta h_t). Select the minimum-value point among x_0,...,x_{T-1} by T-1 charged comparisons. This never needs a function value or optimality certificate. Suppose every recorded point has gap g_t>epsilon. Convexity gives ||grad f(x_t)||>=g_t/||x_t-x_*||>=epsilon/(2R), so all estimates satisfy their promise. Smoothness and the global infimum give ||grad f(x)||^2<=2 beta (f(x)-f_*): apply the descent inequality to x-grad f(x)/beta. Consequently <h_t,x_t-x_*>>=g_t/||grad f(x_t)||-2R delta>=(1/sqrt(2)-1/8)R/sqrt(Q). The projection inequality telescopes to (1/T)sum_t <h_t,x_t-x_*><=R^2/(2 eta T)+eta/2=R/sqrt(T)<=R/sqrt(128Q), a contradiction. Thus the tournament output has gap <=epsilon. The deterministic worst-case cost is T O(d log(d/delta))+(T-1)=O(dQ log(dQ)), with universal constants, uniform in d,beta,R,epsilon. The same deterministic strategy is admissible for randomized g1, with success probability one; no random selection or amplification is needed. This also avoids the t=0 step-size notation in the printed Algorithm 3. Cutting-plane audit: v1 Theorem 1 requires a genuine lower bound gamma on the gradient norm. Theorem 3 (printed p9) instead supplies gamma=sqrt(2 beta epsilon); its displayed convexity argument supplies only gap/(2R) (or gap/(3R) for a general point in B_{2R}), which does not imply that gamma. Explicit admissible witness for Q>=32: f(x)=(2epsilon/R^2)||x-R e_1||^2. Its gradient Lipschitz constant 4epsilon/R^2 is <=beta, its minimizer is R e_1, and at x=0 it has gap 2epsilon and gradient norm 4epsilon/R < sqrt(2 beta epsilon). Thus a nonoptimal query need not satisfy the estimator's promise. Also the full epsilon/2-sublevel need not be bounded by B_{2R}; the constant objective is a simple example. A valid localization proof must intersect with a known ball and handle its boundary. Finally, the displayed cost is [C d log(dR/r_K)] times [O(d log(d/delta))] plus a tournament. With r_K=R/sqrt(Q) and delta=1/(16sqrt(Q)), its direct product is O(d^2 log^2(dQ)), not the claimed single logarithm. These are failures of the supplied justification, not a theorem that the true minimax upper rate cannot be smaller. Quarantine the combined b1 claims; do not adopt a repaired cutting-plane rate without a complete new localization/separation proof. Endpoint checks: R,beta,epsilon are positive and d>=1, so there is no Q=0 endpoint in the contract. Smoothness at x_* gives f(0)-f_*<=beta R^2/2; hence returning 0 uses zero queries when Q<=2. This elementary check is outside all four registered comparison regions and is not added here as a native endpoint bound/comparison. For Q>=32 our fixed schedule applies also at d=1, with no precision-independent saturation assertion. At Q=d^2 the c1/c2 lower formulas both equal Omega(d^2); c1 owns equality.

/proofs/2/body · SHA-256 6b526c69c96b7f3f68ebd9b2f859cdafee6fe1a07c8ac93069a4d7b296a3fe83
# O01: Center-of-gravity cutting upper bound and comparison-tree packing lower bound (guided analyst derivation, pending independent review) This candidate retains the previously questioned min upper bound in quarantine and does not retroactively endorse 2405.11454v1 Theorem3. Direction estimation uses only the independent fixed-length construction already accepted in previous-baseline/proofs/1: given public γ>0 and 0<δ≤1, if ||∇f(x)||≥γ, it returns a unit vector h with error ≤δ using C_dir(d,δ)=2d−1+(d−1)ceil(log2(32sqrt(d)/δ)) comparisons; even when the promise is not satisfied, it always terminates and returns a unit vector. Native tie0 is mapped to +; all step sizes are finite and positive. ## Upper bound under the exact source guard Q≥32 Let Q=βR²/ε≥32, r=sqrt(ε/β), and Kε=B(0,2R)∩{f≤f*+ε/2}. Smoothness and a point x*∈B_R give B(x*,r)⊂Kε, because r≤R and ∇f(x*)=0. Starting from C0=B(0,2R), at each iteration take the center of gravity x of the current known convex body, run the direction estimator above with γ=ε/(3R) and δ=1/(48Q), and retain C∩{y:<h,y−x>≤0}. Suppose, for contradiction, that every examined center of gravity has gap>ε. Then ||x−x*||≤3R, convexity gives ||∇f(x)||>ε/(3R), and β-smoothness gives ||∇f(x)||≤3βR. For every y∈Kε, ||y−x||≤4R and \[ \langle h,y-x\rangle \le\frac{f(y)-f(x)}{\|\nabla f(x)\|}+4R\delta <-\frac{\varepsilon}{6\beta R}+\frac{\varepsilon}{12\beta R}<0. \] Thus every bad cut retains the inner ball. The Grünbaum property implies that any halfspace through the center of gravity retains at most 1−1/e of the volume (apply the ≥1/e bound for the opposite halfspace to the full-dimensional convex body). After the fixed number of iterations \[ N=1+\left\lceil\frac{d\log(2\sqrt Q)}{-\log(1-1/e)}\right\rceil \] if all iterations were still bad, the remaining volume would be smaller than that of a ball of radius r, a contradiction. If positive volume disappears earlier, use the fixed fallback point 0 and a dummy schedule thereafter; this branch cannot occur when all iterations are bad, because the inner ball is retained. Zero-volume determination and center-of-gravity computation are measurable internal operations on a known ball and finitely many cuts, and use no free information about the unknown f; the current native contract allows arbitrary measurable strategies and does not charge for internal computation. Finally, use N−1 charged comparisons to select the examined point with the smallest function value. The total per-path cap is N*C_dir(d,δ)+N−1, hence O(d²logQlog(dQ)). The same deterministic algorithm succeeds on every instance and also satisfies rand≥2/3. An exact center of gravity does not imply computational time efficiency. The [Bubeck 2015 arXiv:1405.4980v2 §2.1 Lemma2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1405.4980v2) Grünbaum volume statement and its adjacent proof, on PDF page 19/printed page 246, were actually checked online. No claim is made to have independently reproved the entire geometric theorem. This argument has the same asymptotic order as the preceding evaluator-only upper-followup/addendum; an independent proof suitable for adoption and a native bound candidate are established only in this round, without retroactively adding earlier approval/read credit.

/proofs/3/body · SHA-256 b5f92c8c6b53114b49d04eaa58c1276c73ae0607e1f0d0d664b94e2b8fe0e500
## Direct-comparison packing lower bound under the exact guard Q≥32 Take f_a(x)=β||x−a||²/2 with a∈B_R. The success set is the closed ball B(a,r0), where r0=sqrt(2ε/β). Take a maximal finite packing in B_R whose centers have pairwise distances strictly greater than 2r0. Its balls of radius 2r0 cover B_R, and volume comparison gives M≥(R/(2r0))^d=(Q/8)^(d/2). The success balls are pairwise disjoint. Fix the algorithm’s entire private random seed. A native ternary comparison tree of depth ≤T has at most 3^T leaves; the unique output at a given leaf can succeed for at most one center. Taking expectation over the seed, success≥2/3 for every center implies 3^T≥(2/3)M. Therefore \[ T\ge\frac{(d/2)\log(Q/8)+\log(2/3)}{\log3}. \] For Q≥32,d≥1, the right-hand side is bounded below by a uniform positive constant times dlogQ, so T=Ω(dlogQ). Deterministic algorithms form a subclass. Early stopping can be padded with zero-tie queries without changing the T cap; outputs need not have been queried, and queries may have arbitrary precision/be unbounded, but none of these allowances enlarges the ternary alphabet of each comparison. This proof does not rely on the exact-value multiscale lower bound; the same counting argument cannot be applied to an exact-value oracle with an infinite real-valued reply alphabet. ## Combination Combining with the retained projected upper bound and the original b3 lower bound under the same guard gives: \[ \Omega(d\max\{\min(d,\sqrt Q),\log Q\})\le T^*\le O(d\min\{Q,d\log Q\}\log(dQ)). \] J1=32≤Q≤d²: the lower bound remains Ω(dsqrtQ), with ratio≤O(min{sqrtQ,dlogQ/sqrtQ}log(dQ)); J2=Q≥32,Q>d²: sqrtQ>logQ ensures that the upper branch reduces to O(d²logQlog(dQ)), the lower bound is Ω(d max{d,logQ}), and ratio≤O(min{d,logQ}log(dQ)), leaving only a polylog gap. Q=d² belongs to J1, and Q=32 includes equality. These are valid envelope/asymptotic-order relations, and crossings of hidden constants are not treated as exact phase transitions. Q<32, the native zero-query registration, and the sharp one-dimensional slice remain separately listed; the previously questioned upper bound remains quarantined.

v1 Theorem 3's supplied gamma does not follow from suboptimality; its product query count also fails to justify a single logarithm. The replacement uses the legitimate gamma and a complete uniform descent proof. /joint_analysis/impact/4/argument · SHA-256 61f9d6148eddfe04b8b6af29ed223a071c0eed5eee1ebec54ed6ba35b412207b
Fresh analyst derivations repair the centroid cutting-plane branch using the accepted finite comparison direction estimator and the independently read Grunbaum volume theorem. A direct ternary-decision-tree packing lower bound supplements the retained value-oracle reduction on Q>=32. Recompute min upper/max lower envelopes; the high-precision c2 gap is logarithmic, the quarantined unsupported single-log source upper remains inactive. This revision addresses the preserved actual independent-review issues. Publication and typed projection obligations are explicit; every mathematical formula and adoption guard is verified against the exact native candidate, and historical effects are not reported as new frontier gains.
